summary: New mission publication supersedes already-active stale runs by default, without overriding existing revision policies. Human-only missions keep person-reviewed proposals; approved cutover creates a fresh linked run at the exact approved revision. When-idle missions wait for their next idle boundary. Replacement admission precedes cancellation; fresh runs retain exact inputs and workspace, wait for ordinary cleanup, and restart every step and program without journal adoption. Incompatible sources remain active with a visible fault. Native and public readers expose supersession lineage alongside retry links.

replay.detail: Append-only mission-run.supersede-linked claims restore both lineage endpoints; reconcile.fault claims in scope mission/supersession restore admission refusals and recovery. Unprotected publication or authorized approved cutover creates a fresh replacement and ordinarily cancels its source atomically only after start admission succeeds. Existing review authorization, exact preview binding, approval recovery, and accepted timestamps remain authoritative. Automatic idle holds reuse canonical revision-draining state and existing work-holder completion; refusal releases the hold. A rebuildable member-local queue observes selected heads, including delayed owned-set promotion. Replacement deadlines start at cleanup admission or retained after-run dependency admission, using accepted timestamps on replay.

schema.detail: Register system-only mission-run.supersede-linked with required source and replacement mission-run references and publication string. Extend mission-run.created with optional phase and admission_publication fields and reconcile.fault with optional publication. Reuse revision-draining for idle holds; replacements use supersession-waiting. Install a rebuildable private v2 head queue at startup before request readers. Its own meta counter preserves finite drain ceilings without adding sqlite_sequence scans to unrelated claim-frontier reads. Initial head seeding, the counter, and a completion witness commit together; interrupted upgrades recover and complete reopens do not write. Views gain optional non-null supersedes, superseded_by, and supersession_fault strings. Generated clients retain retry fields and accept older responses. No destructive data rewrite.

rules.detail: Registry and retention compatibility digests change for supersession contracts. Existing pinned-source human-review and idle-cutover policies take precedence over default automatic supersession; publication cannot remove a source's review protection. Approved proposals keep exact candidate/reviewer/preview fences but create a fresh linked run rather than adopting source work. Native work revision and targeted launch proposal publication atomically include their explicit revision operation before default supersession, retaining authorization and durable direct/proposal responses. Start admissibility, exact input declarations and kinds, capacity, interpolation, and original starter authority are checked before source cancellation. No new DSL grammar, authority grant, or policy knob is introduced.

compatibility.detail: Coordinate participating member upgrades before upgraded owners process stale active runs or new publications, because registry and retention digests change. Startup recovery respects existing review/idle policy. Older tolerant clients ignore additive fields; new clients accept older responses. Unreviewed direct generation adoption remains available; approved proposal responses now name the fresh replacement, not the source. A deliberate same-revision retry after publication remains pinned until a later different definition is published.

downtime.detail: No fleet shutdown or destructive data migration is required. Default publication supersession or approved cutover intentionally cancels an eligible source only after admission succeeds, then waits for ordinary cleanup before replacement work. When-idle policy waits for current work before this cancellation. Human-only policy waits for approval. A replacement admission refusal leaves the source active.

manual.detail: Review fresh-start compatibility before publishing and keep existing review/idle policies where intended; automatic S3 is the default, not an override of those policies. Human-only publication still needs the normal person-approved proposal. Make all steps and program effects idempotent against prior effects. Inspect missions show or public readers for supersedes, superseded_by, supersession_fault, and revision-draining idle holds. Republishing the same revision alone does nothing.

recovery.detail: Supersession does not undo effects or erase source history. If admission fails, inspect both revisions and the incompatibility in supersession_fault, correct the definition, and publish a new revision; refusal releases an automatic idle hold. Resolve ordinary source finalization before replacement work proceeds. Stop new supersession writes before downgrade, retain durable history, and use a compatible owner/reader for in-flight revision-draining or supersession-waiting histories. Restore a compatible build to read new contracts.
